title: Pathfinder
full_review:
Legend has it that half a millennium before Christopher Columbus arrived on our shores, the Vikings did. Of course, for thousands of years beforehand, Native Americans had already called this country home.

In a series of increasingly violent encounters, "Pathfinder" (Fox) attempts to capture the clash between the brutally marauding Norsemen and their prey: tribes of East Coast Wampanoag Indians.

The film starts out promisingly as a Native American woman discovers a Viking shipwreck whose sole survivor is a young blond boy taken in by the initially wary tribe and raised to manhood.

Fifteen years later, Ghost (Karl Urban), as he's now called, is still troubled by sketchy memories of his Viking kinfolk on killing sprees and bears ragged scars on his back for having refused to partake in their gleeful bloodshed.

But this insight is the extent of character development in what amounts to a violent video gamelike movie, courtesy of director Marcus Nispal.

Once the young man returns from a hunting trip to find the Vikings have come back and slaughtered his entire tribe, the movie descends into a straightforward revenge flick. He warns the other tribes, with their inferior bows and arrows, to flee. This includes Pathfinder (Russell Means), a revered shaman, and his daughter Starfire (Moon Bloodgood), who loves the young man and secretly follows him to confront the Vikings.

The Norsemen, indistinguishable from one another in their fearful horned helmets and facial armor, are uniformly and viciously evil. The Native Americans by contrast are all courageously righteous. It remains for Ghost to face down and butcher scores of better-armed warriors. Hardly credible.

Yet credit must be given for the impressive, wintry visuals which capture a nation of, as yet, spectacularly unspoiled natural beauty and a stunning avalanche scene which figures into the plot.

However, the legendary -- if not historical -- aspects of the story are overwhelmed by the unrelenting scenes of gory decapitations, impalings and eviscerations that fuel this shallow salute to murderous revenge.

The film contains excessive violence and gore. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is O -- morally offensive. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted. Under 17 requires accompanying parent or adult guardian.
